sections.title: Prefer stdlib + pflag; dependencies need justification
sections.content: Cobra's only hard deps are pflag (flags) and mousetrap (windows). New dependencies bloat every downstream CLI — additions need maintainer sign-off.

sections.title: Active help must degrade cleanly without env support
sections.content: Active help emits via completion machinery; it must no-op when COBRA_ACTIVE_HELP=0 or the shell lacks support — never break completion to deliver hints.

sections.title: Completion changes must cover bash, zsh, fish, powershell
sections.content: The four *_completions.go generators plus the hidden __complete machinery must stay in sync — a fix in one shell's output without the others is a regression.

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun
sections.content: command.go execute() runs them in that order. Persistent*Run hooks inherit down the tree — a child without its own PersistentPreRun gets the parent's. All hooks only fire if the command declares Run/RunE. Note the asymmetry: parent PersistentPreRun fires for children, but PersistentPostRun runs only if the *executed* command's chain reaches it.

Commands form a tree resolved by ExecuteC and find()
sections.content: Command is a node: root.Execute() -> ExecuteC walks args via find() to resolve the target subcommand, then calls execute(). TraverseChildren controls whether args are parsed as flags during descent or treated strictly as command names until the target is found.

sections.title: Regenerate doc/ output when commands change
sections.content: Man/markdown/yaml docs are generated from the live command tree — stale generated docs are a defect. Re-run the generator after command/flag changes.

sections.title: PersistentFlags inherit to children; local Flags do not
sections.content: cmd.PersistentFlags() propagate down the whole subtree — the idiomatic place for --verbose/--config style globals. Local flags on Flags() apply only to that command. InheritedFlags()/LocalFlags() split them for introspection and help output.

sections.title: Commands form a tree resolved by ExecuteC and find()
sections.content: Command is a node: root.Execute() -> ExecuteC walks args via find() to resolve the target subcommand, then calls execute(). TraverseChildren controls whether args are parsed as flags during descent or treated strictly as command names until the target is found.

sections.title: SetContext flows ctx through ExecuteC to every hook
sections.content: root.SetContext(ctx) before Execute; every Command.Context() returns it inside Run/hooks. ExecuteContext is the all-in-one entry. Cancellation propagates to command execution — the right way to wire signal handling into a cobra app.

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun
sections.content: command.go execute() runs them in that order. Persistent*Run hooks inherit down the tree — a child without its own PersistentPreRun gets the parent's. All hooks only fire if the command declares Run/RunE. Note the asymmetry: parent PersistentPreRun fires for children, but PersistentPostRun runs only if the *executed* command's chain reaches it.

sections.title: genFishComp
sections.content:
func genFishComp(buf io.StringWriter, name string, includeDesc bool) {
	// Variables should not contain a '-' or ':' character
	nameForVar := name
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, "-", "_")
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, ":", "_")

	compCmd := ShellCompRequestCmd
	if !includeDesc {
		compCmd = ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd
	}
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("# fish completion for %-36s -*- shell-script -*-\n", name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`
function __%[1]s_debug
    set -l file "$BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE"
    if test -n "$file"
        echo "$argv" >> $file
    end
end

function __%[1]s_perform_completion
    __%[1]s_debug "Starting __%[1]s_perform_completion"

    # Extract all args except the last one
    set -l args (commandline -opc)
    # Extract the last arg and escape it in case it is a space or wildcard
    set -l lastArg (string escape -- (commandline -ct))

    __%[1]s_debug "args: $args"
    __%[1]s_debug "last arg: $lastArg"

    # Disable ActiveHelp which is not supported for fish shell
    set -l requestComp "%[10]s=0 $args[1] %[3]s $(string join ' ' -- (string escape -- $args[2..-1])) $lastArg"

    __%[1]s_debug "Calling $requestComp"
    set -l results (eval $requestComp 2> /dev/null)

    # Some programs may output extra empty lines after the directive.
    # Let's ignore them or else it will break completion.
    # ...

Never ship a hook-only command
sections.content: PreRun/PersistentPreRun only execute when Run/RunE is declared. A command intended to do work must declare Run — otherwise the hooks silently never fire.

sections.title: Do not put cleanup in root PersistentPostRun expecting it to run for children
sections.content: Cleanup shared across subcommands belongs in each command's own PostRun or a wrapper around Execute — PersistentPostRun on root does not reliably cover children.

sections.title: Commands form a tree resolved by ExecuteC and find()
sections.content: Command is a node: root.Execute() -> ExecuteC walks args via find() to resolve the target subcommand, then calls execute(). TraverseChildren controls whether args are parsed as flags during descent or treated strictly as command names until the target is found.

sections.title: SetContext flows ctx through ExecuteC to every hook
sections.content: root.SetContext(ctx) before Execute; every Command.Context() returns it inside Run/hooks. ExecuteContext is the all-in-one entry. Cancellation propagates to command execution — the right way to wire signal handling into a cobra app.

sections.title: Only persistent flags propagate to subcommands
sections.content: Local flags declared via Flags() stay on their command; PersistentFlags() are visible to the whole subtree.

sections.title: E-suffixed hooks return errors; plain variants do not
sections.content: RunE/PreRunE/PostRunE/PersistentPreRunE/PersistentPostRunE return error, propagated to ExecuteC's return. Plain Run/PreRun/etc return nothing. If both are set the E variant wins. Non-E hooks are for commands that handle errors internally.

sections.title: Cobra runs hooks around Run in a fixed order
sections.content: PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun — persistent variants inherit to children that don't declare their own.

sections.title: Active help streams hints into shell completion
sections.content: active_help.go: programs set messages via GetActiveHelpConfig/ActiveHelp; the __complete machinery emits them as completion descriptions. Controlled by the COBRA_ACTIVE_HELP env var (0 disables, 'local' limits to local commands).

sections.title: Security issues go through SECURITY.md contact, not public issues
sections.content: Per SECURITY.md — report vulnerabilities privately. Public issues for security bugs leak exploit surface.

sections.title: Do not put cleanup in root PersistentPostRun expecting it to run for children
sections.content: Cleanup shared across subcommands belongs in each command's own PostRun or a wrapper around Execute — PersistentPostRun on root does not reliably cover children.

sections.title: PersistentFlags inherit to children; local Flags do not
sections.content: cmd.PersistentFlags() propagate down the whole subtree — the idiomatic place for --verbose/--config style globals. Local flags on Flags() apply only to that command. InheritedFlags()/LocalFlags() split them for introspection and help output.

sections.title: PersistentFlags vs Flags: inheritance boundary
sections.content: Anything meant for the whole CLI goes on PersistentFlags — Flags() definitions are per-command only.

sections.title: Hooks never fire on commands without Run
sections.content: A Command with only PersistentPreRun and no Run/RunE is a no-op — the whole hook chain is gated on Run being declared. Adding a stub Run is required for hook-only commands.

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun

sections.title: Do not put cleanup in root PersistentPostRun expecting it to run for children
sections.content: Cleanup shared across subcommands belongs in each command's own PostRun or a wrapper around Execute — PersistentPostRun on root does not reliably cover children.

sections.title: PersistentFlags inherit to children; local Flags do not
sections.content: cmd.PersistentFlags() propagate down the whole subtree — the idiomatic place for --verbose/--config style globals. Local flags on Flags() apply only to that command. InheritedFlags()/LocalFlags() split them for introspection and help output.

sections.title: PersistentFlags vs Flags: inheritance boundary
sections.content: Anything meant for the whole CLI goes on PersistentFlags — Flags() definitions are per-command only.

sections.title: Hooks never fire on commands without Run
sections.content: A Command with only PersistentPreRun and no Run/RunE is a no-op — the whole hook chain is gated on Run being declared. Adding a stub Run is required for hook-only commands.

Never ship a hook-only command
sections.content: PreRun/PersistentPreRun only execute when Run/RunE is declared. A command intended to do work must declare Run — otherwise the hooks silently never fire.

sections.title: Commands form a tree resolved by ExecuteC and find()
sections.content: Command is a node: root.Execute() -> ExecuteC walks args via find() to resolve the target subcommand, then calls execute(). TraverseChildren controls whether args are parsed as flags during descent or treated strictly as command names until the target is found.

sections.title: E-suffixed hooks return errors; plain variants do not
sections.content: RunE/PreRunE/PostRunE/PersistentPreRunE/PersistentPostRunE return error, propagated to ExecuteC's return. Plain Run/PreRun/etc return nothing. If both are set the E variant wins. Non-E hooks are for commands that handle errors internally.

sections.title: Cobra runs hooks around Run in a fixed order
sections.content: PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun — persistent variants inherit to children that don't declare their own.

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun
sections.content: command.go execute() runs them in that order. Persistent*Run hooks inherit down the tree — a child without its own PersistentPreRun gets the parent's. All hooks only fire if the command declares Run/RunE. Note the asymmetry: parent PersistentPreRun fires for children, but PersistentPostRun runs only if the *executed* command's chain reaches it.

Never ship a hook-only command
sections.content: PreRun/PersistentPreRun only execute when Run/RunE is declared. A command intended to do work must declare Run — otherwise the hooks silently never fire.

sections.title: Shared flags must be PersistentFlags on the root command
sections.content: If a flag should work on every subcommand, declare it via root.PersistentFlags() — local Flags() never inherit.

sections.title: Do not put cleanup in root PersistentPostRun expecting it to run for children
sections.content: Cleanup shared across subcommands belongs in each command's own PostRun or a wrapper around Execute — PersistentPostRun on root does not reliably cover children.

sections.title: Test commands via SetArgs + SetOut/SetErr buffers
sections.content: The idiom: cmd.SetArgs([]string{...}), cmd.SetOut(buf), cmd.SetErr(buf), then Execute(). Works without subprocess; assert on buf contents and the returned error. Remember a fresh command instance per test — flag state persists across Execute calls.

sections.title: SilenceUsage and SilenceErrors control post-error output
sections.content: Command.SilenceUsage suppresses usage printing on error; SilenceErrors suppresses the error echo. Common pattern: SilenceUsage=true once execution has started (usage spam only makes sense for parse errors). Root-level silence gives the app full control of error formatting.

sections.title: Cobra runs hooks around Run in a fixed order
sections.content: PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun — persistent variants inherit to children that don't declare their own.

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun
sections.content: command.go execute() runs them in that order. Persistent*Run hooks inherit down the tree — a child without its own PersistentPreRun gets the parent's. All hooks only fire if the command declares Run/RunE. Note the asymmetry: parent PersistentPreRun fires for children, but PersistentPostRun runs only if the *executed* command's chain reaches it.

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun
sections.content: command.go execute() runs them in that order. Persistent*Run hooks inherit down the tree — a child without its own PersistentPreRun gets the parent's. All hooks only fire if the command declares Run/RunE. Note the asymmetry: parent PersistentPreRun fires for children, but PersistentPostRun runs only if the *executed* command's chain reaches it.

func writePostscript(buf io.StringWriter, name string) {
	name = strings.ReplaceAll(name, ":", "__")
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("__start_%s()\n", name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`{
    local cur prev words cword split
    declare -A flaghash 2>/dev/null || :
    declare -A aliashash 2>/dev/null || :
    if declare -F _init_completion >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        _init_completion -s || return
    else
        __%[1]s_init_completion -n "=" || return
    fi

    local c=0
    local flag_parsing_disabled=
    local flags=()
    local two_word_flags=()
    local local_nonpersistent_flags=()
    local flags_with_completion=()
    local flags_completion=()
    local commands=("%[1]s")
    local command_aliases=()
    local must_have_one_flag=()
    local must_have_one_noun=()
    local has_completion_function=""

sections.title: SetContext flows ctx through ExecuteC to every hook
sections.content: root.SetContext(ctx) before Execute; every Command.Context() returns it inside Run/hooks. ExecuteContext is the all-in-one entry. Cancellation propagates to command execution — the right way to wire signal handling into a cobra app.

sections.content: Cleanup shared across subcommands belongs in each command's own PostRun or a wrapper around Execute — PersistentPostRun on root does not reliably cover children.

sections.title: Positional arg validation runs between flag parsing and Run
sections.content: args.go provides composable validators: NoArgs, ArbitraryArgs, OnlyValidArgs, MinimumNArgs, MaximumNArgs, ExactArgs, RangeArgs, MatchAll, ExactValidArgs. Command.Args is invoked in execute() after flags are parsed; a validator error triggers usage output.

sections.title: Commands form a tree resolved by ExecuteC and find()
sections.content: Command is a node: root.Execute() -> ExecuteC walks args via find() to resolve the target subcommand, then calls execute(). TraverseChildren controls whether args are parsed as flags during descent or treated strictly as command names until the target is found.

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun
sections.content: command.go execute() runs them in that order. Persistent*Run hooks inherit down the tree — a child without its own PersistentPreRun gets the parent's. All hooks only fire if the command declares Run/RunE. Note the asymmetry: parent PersistentPreRun fires for children, but PersistentPostRun runs only if the *executed* command's chain reaches it.

sections.title: Cobra runs hooks around Run in a fixed order
sections.content: PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun — persistent variants inherit to children that don't declare their own.

sections.title: Hook lifecycle: persistent-pre, pre, run, post, persistent-post
sections.content: execute() in command.go fires PersistentPreRun then PreRun before Run, then PostRun and PersistentPostRun. Hooks are gated on Run being declared.

sections.title: Hooks never fire on commands without Run
sections.content: A Command with only PersistentPreRun and no Run/RunE is a no-op — the whole hook chain is gated on Run being declared. Adding a stub Run is required for hook-only commands.

sections.title: Never ship a hook-only command
sections.content: PreRun/PersistentPreRun only execute when Run/RunE is declared. A command intended to do work must declare Run — otherwise the hooks silently never fire.

sections.title: E-suffixed hooks return errors; plain variants do not
sections.content: RunE/PreRunE/PostRunE/PersistentPreRunE/PersistentPostRunE return error, propagated to ExecuteC's return. Plain Run/PreRun/etc return nothing. If both are set the E variant wins. Non-E hooks are for commands that handle errors internally.

sections.title: Only persistent flags propagate to subcommands
sections.content: Local flags declared via Flags() stay on their command; PersistentFlags() are visible to the whole subtree.

sections.title: SetContext flows ctx through ExecuteC to every hook
sections.content: root.SetContext(ctx) before Execute; every Command.Context() returns it inside Run/hooks. ExecuteContext is the all-in-one entry. Cancellation propagates to command execution — the right way to wire signal handling into a cobra app.

Never ship a hook-only command
sections.content: PreRun/PersistentPreRun only execute when Run/RunE is declared. A command intended to do work must declare Run — otherwise the hooks silently never fire.

sections.title: Do not put cleanup in root PersistentPostRun expecting it to run for children
sections.content: Cleanup shared across subcommands belongs in each command's own PostRun or a wrapper around Execute — PersistentPostRun on root does not reliably cover children.

sections.title: PersistentFlags inherit to children; local Flags do not
sections.content: cmd.PersistentFlags() propagate down the whole subtree — the idiomatic place for --verbose/--config style globals. Local flags on Flags() apply only to that command. InheritedFlags()/LocalFlags() split them for introspection and help output.

sections.title: Commands form a tree resolved by ExecuteC and find()
sections.content: Command is a node: root.Execute() -> ExecuteC walks args via find() to resolve the target subcommand, then calls execute(). TraverseChildren controls whether args are parsed as flags during descent or treated strictly as command names until the target is found.

sections.title: E-suffixed hooks return errors; plain variants do not
sections.content: RunE/PreRunE/PostRunE/PersistentPreRunE/PersistentPostRunE return error, propagated to ExecuteC's return. Plain Run/PreRun/etc return nothing. If both are set the E variant wins. Non-E hooks are for commands that handle errors internally.

sections.title: Cobra runs hooks around Run in a fixed order
sections.content: PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun — persistent variants inherit to children that don't declare their own.

Unknown-command suggestions use Levenshtein distance
sections.content: command.go: when find() fails, cobra suggests 'did you mean' candidates at edit distance <= SuggestionsMinimumDistance (default 2). SuggestFor adds explicit aliases that are suggested but not runnable. ld() implements the distance.
sections.graph_path_description: command.go → auto references → Unknown-command suggestions use Levenshtein distance

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun
sections.content: command.go execute() runs them in that order. Persistent*Run hooks inherit down the tree — a child without its own PersistentPreRun gets the parent's. All hooks only fire if the command declares Run/RunE. Note the asymmetry: parent PersistentPreRun fires for children, but PersistentPostRun runs only if the *executed* command's chain reaches it.

sections.content:
func Gt(a interface{}, b interface{}) bool {
	var left, right int64
	av := reflect.ValueOf(a)

	switch av.Kind() {
	case reflect.Array, reflect.Chan, reflect.Map, reflect.Slice:
		left = int64(av.Len())
	case reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:
		left = av.Int()
	case reflect.String:
		left, _ = strconv.ParseInt(av.String(), 10, 64)
	}

	bv := reflect.ValueOf(b)

	switch bv.Kind() {
	case reflect.Array, reflect.Chan, reflect.Map, reflect.Slice:
		right = int64(bv.Len())
	case reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:
		right = bv.Int()
	case reflect.String:
		right, _ = strconv.ParseInt(bv.String(), 10, 64)
	}

	return left > right
}

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun
sections.content: command.go execute() runs them in that order. Persistent*Run hooks inherit down the tree — a child without its own PersistentPreRun gets the parent's. All hooks only fire if the command declares Run/RunE. Note the asymmetry: parent PersistentPreRun fires for children, but PersistentPostRun runs only if the *executed* command's chain reaches it.

Never ship a hook-only command
sections.content: PreRun/PersistentPreRun only execute when Run/RunE is declared. A command intended to do work must declare Run — otherwise the hooks silently never fire.

sections.title: Do not put cleanup in root PersistentPostRun expecting it to run for children
sections.content: Cleanup shared across subcommands belongs in each command's own PostRun or a wrapper around Execute — PersistentPostRun on root does not reliably cover children.

sections.title: PersistentFlags inherit to children; local Flags do not
sections.content: cmd.PersistentFlags() propagate down the whole subtree — the idiomatic place for --verbose/--config style globals. Local flags on Flags() apply only to that command. InheritedFlags()/LocalFlags() split them for introspection and help output.

sections.title: Commands form a tree resolved by ExecuteC and find()
sections.content: Command is a node: root.Execute() -> ExecuteC walks args via find() to resolve the target subcommand, then calls execute(). TraverseChildren controls whether args are parsed as flags during descent or treated strictly as command names until the target is found.

sections.title: SetContext flows ctx through ExecuteC to every hook
sections.content: root.SetContext(ctx) before Execute; every Command.Context() returns it inside Run/hooks. ExecuteContext is the all-in-one entry. Cancellation propagates to command execution — the right way to wire signal handling into a cobra app.

sections.title: E-suffixed hooks return errors; plain variants do not
sections.content: RunE/PreRunE/PostRunE/PersistentPreRunE/PersistentPostRunE return error, propagated to ExecuteC's return. Plain Run/PreRun/etc return nothing. If both are set the E variant wins. Non-E hooks are for commands that handle errors internally.

sections.title: Active help streams hints into shell completion
sections.content: active_help.go: programs set messages via GetActiveHelpConfig/ActiveHelp; the __complete machinery emits them as completion descriptions. Controlled by the COBRA_ACTIVE_HELP env var (0 disables, 'local' limits to local commands).

    __%[1]s_debug "Starting __%[1]s_perform_completion"

    set -l args (commandline -opc)
    # Extract the last arg and escape it in case it is a space or wildcard

    __%[1]s_debug "args: $args"
    __%[1]s_debug "last arg: $lastArg"

func genBashComp(buf io.StringWriter, name string, includeDesc bool) {
	compCmd := ShellCompRequestCmd
	if !includeDesc {
		compCmd = ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd
	}

	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`# bash completion V2 for %-36[1]s -*- shell-script -*-

__%[1]s_debug()
{
    if [[ -n ${BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE-} ]]; then
        echo "$*" >> "${BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE}"
    fi
}

# Macs have bash3 for which the bash-completion package doesn't include
# _init_completion. This is a minimal version of that function.
__%[1]s_init_completion()
{
    COMPREPLY=()
    _get_comp_words_by_ref "$@" cur prev words cword
}

# This function calls the %[1]s program to obtain the completion
# results and the directive.  It fills the 'out' and 'directive' vars.
__%[1]s_get_completion_results() {
    local requestComp lastParam lastChar args

    # Prepare the command to request completions for the program.
    # Calling ${words[0]} instead of directly %[1]s allows handling aliases
    args=("${words[@]:1}")
    requestComp="${words[0]} %[2]s ${args[*]}"

    lastParam=${words[$((${#words[@]}-1))]}
    lastChar=${lastParam:$((${#lastParam}-1)):1}
    __%[1]s_debug "lastParam ${lastParam}, lastChar ${lastChar}"

    if [[ -z ${cur} && ${lastChar} != = ]]; then
        # If the last parameter is complete (there is a space following it)
        # We add an extra empty parameter so we can indicate this to the go method.

sections.title: Do not put cleanup in root PersistentPostRun expecting it to run for children
sections.content: Cleanup shared across subcommands belongs in each command's own PostRun or a wrapper around Execute — PersistentPostRun on root does not reliably cover children.

sections.title: PersistentFlags inherit to children; local Flags do not
sections.content: cmd.PersistentFlags() propagate down the whole subtree — the idiomatic place for --verbose/--config style globals. Local flags on Flags() apply only to that command. InheritedFlags()/LocalFlags() split them for introspection and help output.

sections.title: PersistentFlags vs Flags: inheritance boundary
sections.content: Anything meant for the whole CLI goes on PersistentFlags — Flags() definitions are per-command only.

sections.content:
func writePostscript(buf io.StringWriter, name string) {
	name = strings.ReplaceAll(name, ":", "__")
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("__start_%s()\n", name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`{
    local cur prev words cword split
    declare -A flaghash 2>/dev/null || :
    declare -A aliashash 2>/dev/null || :
    if declare -F _init_completion >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        _init_completion -s || return
    else
        __%[1]s_init_completion -n "=" || return
    fi

    local c=0
    local flag_parsing_disabled=
    local flags=()
    local two_word_flags=()
    local local_nonpersistent_flags=()
    local flags_with_completion=()
    local flags_completion=()
    local commands=("%[1]s")
    local command_aliases=()
    local must_have_one_flag=()
    local must_have_one_noun=()
    local has_completion_function=""
    local last_command=""
    local nouns=()
    local noun_aliases=()

    __%[1]s_handle_word
}

`, name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`if [[ $(type -t compopt) = "builtin" ]]; then
    complete -o default -F __start_%s %s
else
    complete -o default -o nospace -F __start_%s %s
fi

`, name, name, name, name))

Do not put cleanup in root PersistentPostRun expecting it to run for children
sections.content: Cleanup shared across subcommands belongs in each command's own PostRun or a wrapper around Execute — PersistentPostRun on root does not reliably cover children.

sections.title: SetContext flows ctx through ExecuteC to every hook
sections.content: root.SetContext(ctx) before Execute; every Command.Context() returns it inside Run/hooks. ExecuteContext is the all-in-one entry. Cancellation propagates to command execution — the right way to wire signal handling into a cobra app.
